subject: Materials Science
title: Titanium Dioxide Nanoparticles
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Titanium Dioxide Nanoparticles.

hook.text: The white in your sunscreen is TiO₂ nanoparticles — they block UV light while appearing invisible on skin.

buildup.text: Bulk TiO₂ is a brilliant white pigment — but sub-50 nm particles are transparent to visible light while blocking UV.

discovery.text: TiO₂ is a photocatalyst — UV light generates electron-hole pairs that break down organic pollutants on its surface.

twist.text: That photocatalytic activity can generate free radicals on skin — so sunscreen TiO₂ is coated with silica.

climax.text: Self-cleaning windows, air purifiers, and UV-protective coatings all use TiO₂ photocatalysis — sunlight does the work.

punchline.text: One nanoparticle protects skin and cleans buildings — all powered by sunlight.

quiz.question: Why are TiO₂ nanoparticles transparent in sunscreen?
options: Particles below 50 nm are too small to scatter visible light but still absorb UV
They are dyed to match skin tone
